hints: Think about what rate of reaction really means, how fast reactants are used up and how fast products form.
Statements 1 and 2 are the textbook definitions of rate in terms of concentration change per unit time for reactants and products.
Consider whether gas volume change at constant pressure can track product formation, and what that means for all three statements together.
walkthrough:
**Recall what reaction rate means**

Think of rate as speed of chemical change. As time passes, reactants disappear and products appear, so we can follow either side.

Rate rule:
$$\text{rate} = \frac{\text{change in concentration}}{\text{time}}$$

**Check statements 1 and 2**

Statement 1 follows a reactant disappearing, so concentration falls with time. Statement 2 follows a product appearing, so concentration rises with time. Both are standard ways to express rate.

$$\text{rate} = -\frac{\Delta[\text{reactant}]}{\Delta t} = +\frac{\Delta[\text{product}]}{\Delta t}$$

**Check statement 3**

If a gas is produced, the total volume of gas at constant pressure increases as the reaction proceeds. Measuring volume per unit time is just another way of measuring how fast product appears.

$$\text{rate} \propto \frac{\Delta V_{\text{gas}}}{\Delta t} \text{ (at constant p)}$$

**Combine the conclusion**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all valid ways to follow the progress of a reaction, all three can be used to measure rate.

options.A: Correct, because 1, 2 and 3 are all valid. Decrease in reactant concentration and increase in product concentration define rate, and gas volume increase at constant pressure directly tracks moles of gaseous product formed.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statement 3. Students choose this if they think only concentration changes count, forgetting that gas volume is proportional to moles of gas and is a common practical method.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statement 1. Students choose this if they focus only on products appearing and forget that following the disappearance of reactants is equally valid.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination leaves out one or more valid methods. Every statement describes a change per unit time that reflects reaction progress, so no valid method should be excluded.
